title: ASNPC: An Automated Generation Framework for SNN and Neuromorphic Processor Co-Design
problem: SNN and neuromorphic processor design typically prioritize single optimization criterion; hardware-algorithm codesign space is vast with expensive function evaluations.
motivation: Energy-efficient neuromorphic computing requires joint optimization of algorithm and hardware to reduce resource usage while maintaining performance.
method: ASNPC uses a prediction model to efficiently search through the vast space of SNN-processor design options without needing expensive hardware simulations. It automatically generates hardware code (RTL, which describes exactly how the processor's circuits work) for the most promising designs and feeds their performance results back into the search. Over multiple iterations, this discovers a set of good designs where each makes different trade-offs between competing goals like speed, energy efficiency, and accuracy.
key_novelty: Combining a prediction model for exploring multiple design trade-offs with automatic hardware code generation enables efficient SNN-processor co-design.
contributions: ASNPC hardware-algorithm codesign framework for SNNs
Automatic RTL code generation from hardware templates
Better Pareto solutions with lower resource usage and higher throughput vs existing works
limitations: Specific benchmark results and design space characteristics not detailed in abstract.
primary_theme: hardware-algorithm codesign for SNNs via multi-objective optimization
